P.t: Jewish History on the Rocks: Gangsters
P.desc: Grab a drink and uncover the surprising story of Jewish gangsters in early 20th-century America. Explore the rise of organized crime, the unexpected role mob figures played in protecting Jewish communities, and their lasting impact on cities like Las Vegas. Each class pairs Jewish history with a themed craft cocktail.

P.t: Heroes and Villains of the Torah: Timeless Characters, Timeless Lessons
P.desc: Who are the heroes and villains of the Torah — and is it really that simple? Explore unforgettable figures like Abraham, Sarah, Moses, Miriam, Pharaoh, and Jezebel through biblical texts and Jewish interpretation. Discover their strengths, flaws, and complex choices while uncovering timeless lessons about leadership, morality, faith, family, and the human experience.

P.t: Sacred Intimacy: Exploring Sex and Relationships in Jewish Tradition
P.desc: Explore what Jewish tradition teaches about love, relationships, intimacy, and ethics through engaging Talmudic texts and thoughtful discussion. Discover timeless wisdom on one of Judaism's most fascinating and relevant topics.

P.t: Jews in the Neighborhood: Tracing Dallas' Jewish Roots
P.desc: Discover the story of Jewish Dallas through four engaging sessions exploring the people, neighborhoods, and institutions that shaped the city's Jewish community. P.t: Jewish History on the Rocks: Ahoy
P.desc: Set sail for a spirited evening uncovering the remarkable true stories of Jewish pirates who sailed the Caribbean, challenged empires, and fought for survival and freedom. Discover how Sephardic seafarers left their mark on history while enjoying a themed craft cocktail inspired by their adventures.

P.t: Beyond the Books: Author Series at The J
P.desc: Go beyond the pages and into the stories behind them. Beyond the Books: Author Series at the J brings acclaimed writers, thought leaders, and compelling storytellers to the J for engaging conversations about their work, ideas, and the experiences that inspire them. ‍ Each event features author presentations, moderated discussions, audience Q&A, and opportunities for book signings. Whether you're a lifelong reader or simply enjoy thoughtful conversation, this series offers inspiring insights and unforgettable literary experiences.

P.t: For the Love of a Woman
P.desc: The Story: When a mysterious letter arrives after her mother's death, Esther journeys from America to Israel to uncover a hidden family secret. As past and present intertwine, she discovers a powerful story of love, identity, and choices that echo across generations.

The Story: As his Bar Mitzvah approaches, thirteen-year-old Ethan Bloom finds himself questioning faith, identity, and where he truly belongs. Filled with humor and heart, this coming-of-age story follows one boy's unexpected spiritual journey toward self-discovery.

The Story: When her son is born with a club foot, Esther refuses to accept the limitations others place before him. Spanning decades, this inspiring true story celebrates a mother's unwavering determination, resilience, and the extraordinary power of unconditional love.

P.t: Dust Bowls and Jewish Souls: Another Side of Woody Guthrie
P.desc: The Story: Discover the little-known Jewish influence behind legendary songwriter Woody Guthrie. Through music, history, and personal relationships, this documentary reveals how New York's vibrant Jewish community shaped the life, legacy, and songs of an American icon.

The Story: Brussels, 1940. As war looms across Europe, a young actress and a gifted radio sound engineer meet inside Belgium's famed broadcasting house. Bound by storytelling and music, their romance unfolds against the growing uncertainty of a changing world.

The Story: A struggling musician returns to her childhood Jewish summer camp to mentor a quirky group of misfit campers. As the camp faces closure, unexpected friendships, laughter, and teamwork inspire everyone to rediscover the true meaning of community. ‍

P.t: The Road Between Us: The Ultimate Rescue
P.desc: The Story: Retired Israeli General Noam Tibon races into danger to rescue his family during the October 7, 2023 terrorist attacks in Israel. This gripping documentary chronicles courage, sacrifice, and the extraordinary determination to protect loved ones.

The Story: As World War II begins, celebrated pianist François Touraine faces an impossible decision. To save the woman he loves—a Jewish music teacher—he must perform in Germany, confronting impossible choices where love, survival, and morality collide.

The Story: After the birth of her first child, a newly religious woman becomes convinced her husband is no longer the man she married. This compelling mystery explores love, faith, identity, and the quiet transformations that test every relationship. ‍

The Ice Cream Man The Story: Based on an incredible true story, beloved ice cream shop owner Ernst Cahn's courage sparks one of history's largest anti-Nazi protests. This powerful film honors resilience, sacrifice, and the extraordinary impact one person can have against injustice.

‍ Kinder Doll: A Kindertransport Story The Story: Inspired by the Kindertransport rescue mission, this touching story follows two children fleeing Nazi-occupied Europe with only a treasured teddy bear and doll. Their emotional journey captures hope, courage, and the strength to begin again.

Nearly a decade after losing the love of her life, Lucy discovers a hidden clue that leads her to Rome in search of answers about the past. This emotional novel explores grief, family, second chances, and the enduring power of love to shape the future.

Award-winning NBA journalist Yaron Weitzman takes readers behind the scenes of the Los Angeles Lakers and LeBron James era through more than 250 exclusive interviews. This compelling book explores championships, power, leadership, and the business of basketball's most iconic franchise.

Blending timeless Jewish traditions with modern entertaining, A Year of Jewish Joy features more than 75 recipes, creative table settings, and meaningful holiday inspiration. Rebekah Lowin shares practical ideas that help transform Shabbat and every Jewish celebration into memorable gatherings filled with warmth, beauty, and connection. ‍

P.t: The Vet Will See You Now
P.desc: Veterinarian Dr. Barak Benaryeh shares unforgettable patient stories, practical pet care advice, and behind-the-scenes insights from life inside the exam room. Blending humor, compassion, and experience, this engaging book helps readers better understand the animals they love. ‍

Celebrate Jewish holidays through more than 50 creative projects designed for families, classrooms, and communities of all ages. Filled with colorful crafts, thoughtful reflections, and inspiring activities, this book transforms Jewish traditions into meaningful hands-on experiences throughout the year.

Discover 10 beloved Jewish holidays through colorful illustrations, engaging stories, and more than 1,000 hidden objects to find. Filled with fun facts, interactive puzzles, and "Spot the Difference" challenges, this vibrant book offers children and families an entertaining way to learn, celebrate, and explore Jewish traditions together. ‍

After her mother's dementia diagnosis, Glenna Hecht discovered a simple game that transformed caregiving into moments of connection, joy, and meaningful conversation. Part memoir and part practical guide, this inspiring book offers caregivers hope, compassion, and a fresh perspective on dementia.

Psychiatrist Dr. Suzanne Garfinkle-Crowell explores how social media and "therapy speak" are changing the way young women understand themselves and express emotions. Blending clinical insight with compassion, she offers parents and educators valuable tools for today's evolving conversations. ‍

P.t: Memories of a Good Meal: Recipes of Resilience, Inspired by Stories of World War II Survival
P.desc: Combining powerful stories with memorable recipes, this moving book honors Holocaust survivors and World War II heroes through the meals that preserved hope and family traditions. Featuring recipes by James Beard Award-winning chef Alon Shaya, it celebrates resilience, remembrance, and connection.

Florist and clairvoyant Jenny Barker reveals the healing energy and symbolism behind flowers, helping readers create meaningful arrangements for every season of life. Filled with stunning photography and practical guidance, Flower Energy inspires connection, wellness, and intentional living through the beauty of blooms.

P.t: The Chief: The Story of the Boston Celtics' Most Enigmatic Icon
P.desc: NBA Hall of Famer Robert "The Chief" Parish reflects on his remarkable journey from rural Louisiana to four NBA championships and a record-setting 21 seasons in professional basketball. In conversation with longtime Dallas Mavericks broadcaster Chuck Cooperstein , who has covered the NBA for more than three decades and is one of basketball's most respected play-by-play voices. The evening will be introduced by legendary broadcaster Brad Sham .

These classes are for toddlers and parents to play together and explore the gym. Toddlers use the gymnastics equipment to practice developmental activities, such as jumping, rolling, and balancing. The classes focus on enhancing coordination and body awareness while learning to interact with other toddlers and adults. ‍

P.t: Beyond the Pink: Navigating Life, Health and Breast Cancer
P.desc: Written by leading medical oncologist Dr. Eleonora Teplinsky, Beyond the Pink combines expert medical guidance with compassionate support for every stage of the breast cancer journey. In conversation with Kim Holden , a somatic intimacy coach and 21-year breast cancer survivor who helps women reclaim confidence, healing, and connection after life's most difficult chapters.

P.t: Hold on to Your Music, A Mother's Legacy
P.desc: ‍ Hold on to Your Music, A Mother's Legacy ‍ The Story: Three generations of Jewish women confront the lasting impact of the Holocaust through music, memory, and family. Spanning Vienna, London, and Los Angeles, this moving story explores healing, resilience, and the enduring power of legacy.

P.t: A Time to Gather: How Ritual Created the World—and How It Can Save Us
P.desc: In A Time to Gather , bestselling author Bruce Feiler explores the resurgence of rituals that are helping people reconnect in an increasingly fragmented world. Drawing on stories from six continents and more than 100 ritual designers, he reveals how meaningful gatherings can strengthen relationships, celebrate life's milestones, and foster a deeper sense of belonging.

P.t: Israel on Trial: Examining the History, the Evidence, and the Law
P.desc: In this New York Times bestselling book, Judge Roy K. Altman examines today’s most debated claims surrounding Israel through history, international law, and evidence. Blending legal analysis with historical context, he challenges readers to separate facts from rhetoric in today’s complex conversations. Join Judge Roy Altman in conversation with Joel Schwitzer for a timely and thought-provoking discussion that brings these critical issues to life.

With humor, honesty, and expert insight, Millennial Menopause offers a fresh guide to hormonal changes, mental health, careers, relationships, and self-advocacy. It empowers millennial women to navigate menopause with confidence, clarity, and community. Join author Lauren Tetenbaum in conversation with Tara Ohayon for an open, engaging discussion about navigating this next chapter with knowledge and confidence.

P.t: Divine Corners: In the Shadow of the Holocaust on a Catskills Chicken Farm
P.desc: In this illustrated memoir, psychiatrist Michelle Friedman reflects on growing up as the daughter of Holocaust survivors on a remote Catskills chicken farm. Blending family history with personal memories, she explores resilience, Jewish identity, and the lasting impact of trauma across generations.

P.t: Saturday 8:30 AM Beginner/Intermediate Pickleball Drill with Curtis Reese
P.desc: Perfect for players who are new to pickleball and those who have playing experience, this drill focuses on building a strong foundation of skills, knowledge, and confidence.
Child-led, open-gym-style playtimes designed for neurodivergent children. Parents or caregivers stay with their child as they explore the gym at their own pace. $20 members, $25 non-members.

P.desc: Challenge your skills and enjoy spirited competition in the J Dallas Competitive Mahj League. Six Monday sessions (December 8, 15, 22, 29 and January 5, 12), then Championship night on January 19, 2027.

P.days: Three-hour sessions in the Jmahj Room
P.desc: No group? No problem! Come solo, bring a friend, or arrive with your group of four. Solo players are matched with others of similar skill level. Registration required in advance.

Calling all young chefs! Spend eight weeks chopping, sizzling, baking, and exploring flavors from around the world. Build kitchen skills, take on weekly cooking challenges, compete in an ultimate cook-off, and finish the season by making traditional Hanukkah treats to celebrate with family.

P.t: Forgotten and Rediscovered | Jewish Music Between Persecution and Revival
P.desc: Experience a 30-minute piano concert followed by a fascinating lecture exploring Jewish music lost through Nazi persecution and Stalinist repression, and its rediscovery today. Pianist and musicologist Jascha Nemtsov, Professor of the History of Jewish Music at the Liszt University of Music in Weimar, brings these forgotten composers and their remarkable stories back to life.
